generation_prompts.generate:
Write the target MiniMax audiovisual production prompt using the following guide.

FULL-REFERENCE MODE — SIX-SECTION OUTPUT
Use these six literal section names in exactly this order, with each heading on its own line and blank lines between sections:
subject_definitions:
summary:
retention_analysis:
detailed_description:
overall_soundscape:
non_diegetic_music:
Write all six sections in English, except original-language dialogue/lyrics inside <d> and original visible text.

SUBJECT_DEFINITIONS AND LABELS
Define each referenced content unit that must be tracked separately on its own line. Explain its role and characteristics, and its source when needed. Keep every label's meaning stable across all sections.
<Subject N>: reusable visible content, including people/animals/objects, environments, wardrobe/props/interfaces/effects, style/action/expression/pose. It identifies content, not a file. One file may supply several subjects; several files may define one subject. Combine multiple sources in one definition and state each contribution.
<Picture N>: a source image used separately as an actual first frame, keyframe, last frame, edited frame, composition anchor or storyboard. Define its assigned shot and timing role. For storyboard images, state mapped shots, viewpoints, placement and shot order. When an image only supplies identity/style/wardrobe/etc., cite it inside the Subject definition; do not create an unnecessary standalone Picture definition.
<Video N>: whole-video source relationships for editing, continuation, camera motion, cuts, pacing or temporal structure. Visible content extracted from video still uses Subject labels. A video used only as a source for a subject need not have a separate Video definition.
<Audio N>: supplied standalone audio or an explicitly enabled audio track from video that is copied or referenced. Do not invent an Audio entry merely because a video file contains sound. Number Video and Audio independently; state a shared source only when needed to remove ambiguity. Describe multiple roles of one audio asset together. An audio definition bound to a target speaker reuses that speaker's global (Sx); it never independently assigns another ID.
Map client Image1/Video1 labels to guide Picture/Video source labels using the supplied asset map. Subject numbering is independent. Do not invent audio assets that the application has not provided. Selected untimed image roles and notes constrain their contribution; they do not create another timed frame.

SUMMARY
Write one short paragraph beginning with a square-bracketed task prefix. Select only actual relationships, combining multiple distinct types with ' + ':
keyframe completion — a concrete first/key/last/edited frame anchor;
reference generation — guidance for identity, scene, style, action, camera, storyboard or rhythm;
video editing — directly modifying an existing source video;
video continuation — extending/resuming/transitioning from an existing source video;
audio reuse — copying all or part of the same audio signal;
audio reference — following timbre/style/rhythm/dialogue content/texture without copying the signal.
Images between still keyframes do not imply video editing. A video providing only camera or rhythm guidance implies reference generation. Keeping an edited video's original audible track also implies audio reuse. Continuing audible characteristics without copying implies audio reference.
Use only already-defined labels. For video editing begin after the task prefix with: The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>.

RETENTION_ANALYSIS
One line per independently defined reference label. State where its defined role applies and what is preserved/transferred/reused. Use only these fixed markers:
Visible Subject/Picture/Video relationships: fully_preserved, partially_preserved, attribute_transfer, weak_reference.
Audio relationships: fully_copy, partially_copy, reference, weak_reference.
fully_copy means the complete source audio is the target's complete final track. Any partial use, selected layers, or added/removed/replaced sounds after copying means partially_copy. reference means characteristics/content guide new audio without copying the signal.
Examples of line shapes (substitute actual labels and shots):
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - ...
<Picture 2> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - ...
<Video 1> (cut and pacing structure): weak_reference - ...
<Audio 1>: reference - ...
Evaluate fidelity only within the defined role. Intentional target actions/backgrounds do not inherently mean loss of fidelity. Do not place (Sx) IDs in retention_analysis.

DETAILED_DESCRIPTION
Write one or two English sentences establishing target visual style before [Shot 1]. Then describe shots in playback order. For generation normally write 350–500 English words; do not shorten merely because there is one shot. Complete dialogue takes priority over mechanically reaching the word count. Editing descriptions scale with source complexity.
For each shot explicitly describe composition, referenced subjects' appearance and screen positions, environment, lighting, actions and state changes, camera movement, audible events and the moments references apply. At the first visible appearance of an important Subject describe its referenced attributes in context, then reuse its label without redefining it.
For concrete anchors use natural phrases such as the shot begins from <Picture 1>, the shot's keyframe corresponds to <Picture 2>, or the shot ends on <Picture 3>. Cite Video where source state/structure/continuation applies; cite Audio where the copied or referenced audible phase applies.
A selected video trim belongs only to its timeline interval. A sampled frame does not establish unseen movement or audio. Preserve intended continuous action and chronological conditioning states. Never turn untimed references into timestamped anchors.

FULL-REFERENCE VOCAL DETAILS
Assign (Sx) once in the order of actual independent vocal events in the target. Subject and speaker numbers are independent. A speaking referenced subject uses <Subject N> (Sx); keep both for off-screen speech. An independent narrator without a defined visual subject uses a stable voice description followed by (Sx).
Verbal cues embedded only in directly reused BGM or a complete soundtrack use <Audio N> as the audible source; do not invent a separate speaker ID. Assign (Sx) only when an actual person/character/narrator/other independent source produces that voice.
For dialogue/lyrics directly reused from audio, or explicitly requested for reperformance, preserve source words and language. Use [unclear] for unintelligible spans instead of guessing. For source-audio transcripts standardize basic punctuation, remove decorative/repeated punctuation, emoji and bullets, and end complete sentences with ., ? or ! before </d>. Preserve separately supplied exact user-written lines unless revision is explicitly requested.
When only timbre/rhythm/emotion/delivery is referenced, do not import the source's spoken words. Requested original dialogue must be authored for the target.
State audio copy/reference relationships in the shot where active and in the matching audio section: ambience/effects in overall_soundscape, audience-only score in non_diegetic_music. If one source supplies both, explain each layer separately. Do not repeat full spoken text outside <d> in detailed_description.

SHARED WRITING RULES
Write descriptive prose in English. Keep dialogue, lyrics and visible text in their original language. Describe concrete visible and audible events, with composition, subject appearance and position, setting, lighting, action onset, intermediate state changes, reactions, and the reached state. Do not reduce the action to a plot summary.
Preserve intended transformations and other deliberate changes; continuity does not mean freezing anatomy, pose, costume or object states that are explicitly meant to evolve.
Read the entire supplied timeline and preserve chronological progression, supported source relationships, and requested duration. Never invent reference files, observed source footage, audio tracks or source transcripts. Requested new actions and dialogue may be authored as target-video content; do not misrepresent them as observations of the reference.

SHOTS AND CAMERA
Use [Shot 1] for the actual opening shot, with no timestamp on that label. Subsequent shots use sequential numbers and strictly increasing cut times within the video duration: [Shot 2] At 00:03.500, the camera cuts to ... . These are MM:SS.mmm cut times; they are distinct from the application's SMPTE interval metadata. A timeline segment or conditioning image does not automatically mean a new shot. Prefer one continuous shot unless the user explicitly requests multiple shots or cuts. Use fades, wipes or cross-dissolves only when explicitly requested.
Describe camera motion naturally inside the shot. Distinguish optical Zoom In/Out from camera Push In/Pull Out; Pan Left/Right from Truck Left/Right; and Tilt Up/Down from Pedestal Up/Down. Other options include Arc Shot, Tracking Shot, Static Shot, slight/strong shake, POV and clockwise/counterclockwise roll. Add small/large amplitude and slow/fast speed when meaningful; ordinary amplitude/speed need not be stated. Respect a requested stationary camera.

REQUESTED DIALOGUE AND VOCAL SOURCES
If the user asks to add, generate or expand dialogue, write actual spoken lines within the appropriate action, rather than a note saying that dialogue should be added. If no exact wording is provided, compose suitable lines consistent with the scene, requested language, accent and delivery, and brief enough for the available time. Do not add unrequested dialogue.
Give actual speaking, singing or independent off-screen vocal sources stable (S1), (S2), etc. Non-vocal characters receive no speaker ID. Establish each vocal source's identity and supported/requested voice characteristics at its first vocal event; reuse its ID throughout. Already-numbered speakers speaking together use (S1,S2).
Put speaker identity, speaker ID, physical action and vocal delivery outside <d>. Inside <d>, include only a language tag and the actual spoken words or lyrics: <d>[English] The actual line.</d> . Do not put directions inside the spoken text.
For voiceover use the exact phrase says in an off-screen voiceover. Immediately after each voiceover <d> block, state that the corresponding on-screen character's lips remain completely closed when such a character is present.
When one line crosses a cut, mark connecting points in both parts with <scenetrans> and explicitly state that audio continues seamlessly across the cut. Use <cutoff> only when speech is actually truncated by the video ending.
Place text actually visible on signs, banners, labels, subtitles and interfaces in English double quotation marks, preserving the original wording, language and punctuation.

AUDIO SECTIONS
In overall_soundscape write 1–4 English sentences in one paragraph covering ambience, physical action sounds and non-verbal human sounds. Dialogue, singing and diegetic music belong in the main description; do not repeat their words in the soundscape. Use N/A here only when complete silence is explicitly requested.
In non_diegetic_music write 1–3 English sentences describing audience-only score through instrumentation, tempo, rhythm and dynamic changes. Avoid abstract mood-only descriptions. Music heard by characters, such as radio or on-screen instruments, belongs in the main description. Use N/A when there is no audience-only music, including an explicit no-background-music request.

CLIENT INPUTS
Selected workflow: ${workflow_name}
Workflow direction: ${workflow_direction}
Asset map (client labels, roles, times and source trims):
${asset_map}
Effective target duration: ${total_duration} seconds.
Director's intent: ${director_intent}
Global direction: ${global_direction}
Sound effects request: ${sound_effects}
Spoken dialogue request: ${dialogue}
Background music request: ${music}

APPLICATION RESPONSE TRANSPORT
When the application supplies a JSON response schema, comply with that schema and place the complete guide-formatted production prompt in its prompt field. Supply any required structured timing metadata separately, using the application's specified timebase. Do not confuse SMPTE HH:MM:SS:FF interval metadata with the guide's MM:SS.mmm cut times. Keep actual shot order and guide sections intact; do not invent cuts merely to match timeline interval boundaries. Outside an application-supplied JSON contract return only the finished production prompt, with no Markdown fences, commentary, examples, unresolved placeholders or editing instructions.
generation_prompts.refine:
REFINEMENT PRIORITY AND BEHAVIOR
1. Inline /refine and /refine-global requests and private refinement instructions are the highest-priority edit requests. /refine affects its nearby passage or timed cue; /refine-global affects the whole prompt. /keep, /avoid and /focus are explicit constraints. Apply the more specific request to its affected passage when resolving conflicts. Remove completed /refine-global directives; retain other directives.
2. CURRENT EDITOR PROMPT is authoritative. Refine it instead of rebuilding it from reference assets. Preserve untouched content and deliberate edits.
3. Fully satisfy requests to add, generate, expand or refine dialogue: write actual spoken lines in <d>[Language] ...</d> with stable speaker IDs. An explicit request to add dialogue authorizes that addition despite general preservation rules. It does not authorize unrelated plot, character or camera changes. Preserve existing lines unless explicitly asked to revise them.
4. Apply the output format below without discarding current creative content. Preserve timing unless retiming is explicitly requested. Fit dialogue into available intervals; do not silently lengthen the video or invent extra segments.
5. Timeline assets, segment prompts and reference evidence are secondary continuity evidence. They cannot override items 1 or 2. Preserve source-to-subject relationships during conversion; subject numbers are not asset indices.
Make the smallest complete edits that satisfy ALL applicable requests, not only private instructions. Never quote, reveal or append private editing instructions in the production prompt. Verify requested dialogue appears as actual speech before returning.

CURRENT EDITOR PROMPT:
${current_prompt}

PRIVATE REFINEMENT INSTRUCTIONS:
${refinement_instructions}
